pages.text: "Dad, why so slow?" Bami stamped in the cab. Snow covered everything outside, and the train crawled. Bami wanted to reach the last stop and go sledding.
Dad held the big handle. "Snow makes the track slippery. We go slowly to avoid slipping." "Faster!" Bami pouted. Dad winked. "Slow lets you see everything." Bami turned away.
Bami flopped into the dining-car window seat. Same white fields, same slow train. "Boring! When will we get there?" They pecked the glass.
Across from Bami, a fox painter carrying a drawing board opened her paints. "Bored, little conductor? Play a drawing game with me?" Bami looked into the box. "What game?"
"One for slow trains. Look carefully at the snow." She gave Bami paper. Rabbit tracks dotted the white field! "Fast would whisk them past. That's why we go slowly in the snow!"
Holding a brush in a foot, Bami dotted rabbit tracks. "Berries! A snowman!" Tracks, berries, and a snowman filled the paper. Bami repeated, "Go slowly in the snow!"
The fox brushed her board. A little train appeared on the snow, yellow lamps in every window. "Our train!" Bami laughed. Snow outside, snow in the picture—and Bami's train inside it.
Bami put down the brush and spread their wings. "Finished! Our train in the snow!" The irritation was gone. A slow train wasn't boring anymore.
"Last stop!" Pipi called. Holding the picture in a foot, Bami counted. "One, go slowly in snow! Two, look outside! Three, draw each thing! I'll draw again next slow ride!"
Dad came down and hugged Bami. "We came slowly and didn't slip. Now sledding!" Going slowly meant no slipping and more to see. Go slowly in the snow! Bami proudly showed Dad the picture.
